# VoxelService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("VoxelService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

A world made of blocks, for games about mining and building with cubes. It is separate from `Terrain`, which is a smooth sculpted landscape: this is a grid of cubes, each of one block type, with flat axis-aligned faces.

A block is addressed by integer block coordinates, as a `vector`. Block `(0, 0, 0)` extends from the origin to `BlockSize` along every axis. Register the game's block types once, then place and remove blocks by id. Id 0 is air.

The engine draws the blocks and makes them solid. Each chunk is meshed with hidden faces removed and coplanar faces merged, and shaded with ambient occlusion at the corners.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BlockSize` | `number` | `1` | read/write | The size of one block, in meters. It can be set only while the world has no blocks; otherwise setting it raises an error. Call `Clear` first to change it in a built world. |
| `BlockTypeCount` | `number` | — | read-only | The number of registered block types. Their ids run from 1 to this number. |
| `ChunkCount` | `number` | — | read-only | The number of 16 by 16 by 16 chunks that hold at least one block. A chunk with no blocks is not stored. |

## Methods

### `BlockToWorld(block: vector): vector`

Returns the world position of the center of a block.

### `Clear()`

Removes every block. The registered block types are kept.

### `FillBlocks(from: vector, to: vector, id: number): number`

Fills every block in the box between two block coordinates, both included, with one block id; 0 empties the box. Returns the number of blocks that changed. Use it to build a floor, a wall or the first ground of a world in one call. Raises an error for a box of more than 256 blocks along an axis; fill a larger box in pieces.

### `GetBlock(block: vector): number`

Returns the id of the block at a block coordinate, or 0 for air. A fluid block returns the fluid's type at every level; use `GetFluidDepth` for how full it is.

### `GetBlockId(name: string): number?`

Returns the id a block type was registered with, or nil if no type has that name.

### `GetFluidDepth(block: vector): number`

Returns how full a block is with fluid, from 0 to 1. It is 1 where the fluid is falling or has more of the same fluid above it, slightly below 1 at a source, and lower with each block the fluid has spread. Returns 0 for a block that is not a fluid.

### `Raycast(origin: vector, direction: vector): (vector?, vector?)`

Casts a ray through the blocks and returns the first solid block it enters and the face it entered through, as an outward normal. Returns nil and nil if it hits nothing within the length of `direction`. The block is the one to break; the block plus the normal is where to place a new block. Fluids do not stop the ray.

### `RegisterBlock(name: string, color: Color3, sideColor: Color3?, bottomColor: Color3?): number`

Registers a block type and returns its id. Ids are assigned from 1 in the order of registration, so the same script gets the same ids on every machine. Registering a name again returns its existing id and updates its colors. A world can have up to 4,095 block types.

`color` is the color of the top face, and of every face if no other color is given. `sideColor` is the color of the four sides, and `bottomColor` the color of the bottom, which defaults to the side color. A grass block, for example, is green on top and brown elsewhere.

### `SetBlock(block: vector, id: number): boolean`

Places a block, or removes one when `id` is 0. `block` is a block coordinate, whose components are rounded down. Returns whether anything changed.

### `SetBlockFluid(id: number, reach: number, ticksPerStep: number?)`

Makes a block type a fluid, such as water, lava or oil. With a `reach` of 0, it makes the type an ordinary block again.

A fluid block placed with `SetBlock` or `FillBlocks` is a source and stays in place. From it the fluid flows down first, filling every empty block below. Where it cannot fall, it spreads sideways for `reach` blocks (1 to 7), one level shallower with each block. When the source is removed, the fluid it fed drains away. The fluid moves once every `ticksPerStep` simulation ticks (default 5); a larger number makes a slower fluid.

A fluid is drawn translucent whatever its opacity setting, as deep as it is full. It does not collide and does not block `Raycast`, so a character can walk into a lake and a tool can reach the lake bed. `GetBlock` returns the fluid's type at every level, and `GetFluidDepth` returns how full a block is.

### `SetBlockOpacity(id: number, opacity: Enum.BlockOpacity, transparency: number?)`

Sets how a block type lets what is behind it show through. `Cutout` blocks have holes where their image is transparent. `Translucent` blocks blend with what is behind them; `transparency` (0 to 1, default 0.5) sets how much shows through where the image does not. See-through blocks still collide, and they do not darken the corners of the blocks around them.

### `SetBlockTextures(id: number, texture: string, sideTexture: string?, bottomTexture: string?)`

Sets the images of a block type, as content paths such as `asset://textures/grass_top.png`, for its top, its four sides and its bottom. The sides default to the top image and the bottom to the side image. The block's colors tint its images, so register the type in white to show the images unchanged. An empty string removes an image.

Each image fills one face of a block and repeats on every block. Images are sampled without filtering, so pixel art stays sharp at any distance. The side image is upright on every side and is never mirrored.

### `SetFluidReaction(from: number, touching: number, result: number)`

Sets what the fluid `from` turns into where it touches the fluid `touching`. For example, lava that touches water turns to stone, and the water stays. A block of `from`, including a source, that touches `touching` on any of its six sides turns into `result` on the next step.

Both types must be fluids. A `result` of 0 removes the reaction. To make the other fluid change too, set a second reaction with the two types swapped.

### `WorldToBlock(position: vector): vector`

Returns the block coordinate that a world position falls in.
